subject: verify-suite-before-review
body:
## Description

Prove the phase exit criteria hold together: run `orchestra review-brief` through its entry point against a temporary repository, then every other phase check.

## Approach

Add an end-to-end test `test_review_brief_end_to_end` in `tests/test_suite_before_review.py`. It builds a temporary git repository with a required suite policy, runs `cli.main(["review-brief", "--phase", ...])` with no suite check-run and sees exit 2 with the missing check-run named, then records a passing `<phase>-suite` check-run at head and sees the brief printed. Run `tests/test_suite_before_review.py`, `tests/test_phase_end_order.py` and the skill and contract consistency tests. Do not edit the tree.
title: Verify the suite-before-review phase

subject: phase-end-order
body:
## Description

R1: `phase-end.md` runs the suite step before the reviewer step.
R6: `phase-end.md` says a failing required suite creates fix tasks before the reviewer starts.

## Approach

In `skills/execute-phase/references/phase-end.md` change the order line to: last implementation wave, closing verification, analyze, suite, reviewer, integration-report, phase gate, phase close. Move the `## Suite` section above `## Reviewer`. In it say the suite runs at the phase head after analyze, and a failing `gate=required` suite creates fix tasks before the reviewer starts. In `## Reviewer` pass `--phase <phase-slug>` to `orchestra review-brief` and say it refuses until the suite policy is met at the head. Say a fix task moves the head and the suite runs again before the reviewer. Update the matching order sentence in `skills/execute-phase/SKILL.md` step 7. Keep copies of these files in sync if `tests/test_skill_portability.py` or `tests/test_contract_self_consistency.py` pin them.

Write tests in `tests/test_phase_end_order.py`: the suite heading comes before the reviewer heading, the order line lists suite before reviewer, and the fix-task sentence exists.
title: Run the suite before the reviewer in the skills

subject: fix-review-end-to-end
body:
## Description

title: Add the end-to-end review-brief test

subject: brief-suite-check
body:
## Description

R2: `orchestra review-brief` exits non-zero when a local suite is configured but no `<phase>-suite` check-run exists at the phase head.
R3: `orchestra review-brief` exits non-zero when `gate=required` is set but the `<phase>-suite` check-run at the phase head failed.
R4: `orchestra review-brief` builds the brief when `gate=advisory` is set, even if the `<phase>-suite` check-run at the phase head failed.
R5: `orchestra review-brief` builds the brief when `mode=none`, `mode=external` or `gate=deferred`, with no suite check-run.

## Approach

Add `suite_ready_for_review(policy, check_runs, phase_slug, phase_head)` to `orchestra/conductor/suite.py`. It returns a refusal message or an empty string. Use `SuitePolicy.run_locally`, `blocks_merge`, `is_suite_check_run` and the revision match already in that module. Rules: a policy that does not run locally needs nothing. A local policy needs a `<phase>-suite` check-run at the phase head. A `blocks_merge` policy also needs that check-run to pass. An advisory policy accepts a failed check-run.

In `_cmd_review_brief` in `orchestra/cli.py`, call it when `--phase` is given. Load the policy with `suite.load_suite_policy(work)` and the check-runs from the store. Resolve `--phase-head` to a full revision first. On a refusal print `orchestra review-brief: <message>` to stderr and return 2. The message names the missing or failing check-run and the head. Without `--phase` nothing changes.

Write tests in `tests/test_suite_before_review.py` with `brief` in each test name, one per requirement, using the helpers in `tests/test_cli_surface.py`. Run them first and see them fail.
title: Make review-brief enforce the suite policy
